blocks.content: Explore Demo Wind Farm to see the text that introduces the dashboard's purpose, where a panel's description would go, and the link that helps viewers find the next useful view.

blocks.title: Introduction and links on Demo Wind Farm

blocks.content: This text panel near the top introduces the dashboard's purpose: what viewers can learn from it and where to start. It also names the data source. Helpful text like this gives viewers the context they need to understand the dashboard.
Find the **Current Power** panel. Its title says what it shows, and it has no **i** icon, so it has no description.

steps.reftarget: div[data-viz-panel-key='panel-14'] button[data-testid='data-testid Panel menu Current Power']
steps.description: Click here to open the panel menu.
Click Edit to open the panel editor.

blocks.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid Panel options Description field property editor']

blocks.content: This is where a panel's description goes: what the value measures, why it matters, or how to read it alongside another panel. Once a panel has a description, viewers see it behind the small **i** icon in the top left corner of the panel. None of this dashboard's panels has one.

steps.description: Click Back to return to the dashboard.

steps.reftarget: button[data-testid='data-testid Exit edit mode button'], button[data-testid='data-testid Edit dashboard button']
steps.description: The dashboard is still in edit mode. Click Exit edit.

blocks.content: If Grafana asks about unsaved changes, select **Discard**. Nothing needed saving.
View the first link in the dashboard.

A dashboard link is a shortcut at the top of a dashboard that takes viewers to another dashboard or an external website. This one goes to an external website, and its name explains what viewers will find there. Links help viewers choose where to go when they need more detail, and you can add them to your own dashboards.
